activity.notes: After Alexander the Great's death in 323 BCE, Ptolemy son of Lagus established himself as satrap/governor of Egypt under the nominal Argead kings. He governed Egypt in that capacity until taking the royal title in 305 BCE. ATLAS records this pre-royal Egyptian government separately from his existing 305-282 BCE kingship of the Ptolemaic Kingdom.

sources.citation_text: The Oxford Classical Dictionary states that after Alexander's death in 323 BCE Ptolemy established himself as satrap in Egypt and took the title of King in 305 BCE.
